title: CWE-22: Path traversal to a restricted directory
prerequisites: a file or include path built by concatenating or joining attacker-influenced input into a base directory
the input is not resolved and checked against the restricted directory before the filesystem or include call uses it
excerpt: The weakness is that a pathname assembled from caller-supplied input is trusted to stay inside its intended directory, when relative segments or an absolute path let it name a file anywhere the process can reach. A relative form climbs out with repeated parent-directory segments; an absolute form skips the base directory entirely and names the target outright. This is a web request reaching the filesystem through a path it builds, not a host-side tool used after a shell already exists: the effect worth proving is the content of a specific file outside the intended directory, read or included through the vulnerable parameter itself.
